One research field changes: delta_t quantity_id elapsed_time -> duration (physical seconds-denominated duration; elapsed_time is finance-owned and dimensionless in the registry). Symbol, unit s, context, definition, expression delta_Q/delta_t, references, guards, and sources are unchanged. Record now projects runtime-ready with a validating runtime_model.

assumptions: Source definition (Eq. 9.1): charge and elapsed time refer to the same cross section and interval.

Application convention: the orientation is fixed throughout the accounting interval. Include charge moved during every part of the elapsed window; counting only active-time charge requires justification that other periods contribute zero.
No constant-current assumption is needed for the definition. A use as a steady DC value additionally requires current to be constant over the entire interval.

models.inverse_notes: Solve delta_Q given I_avg,delta_t: delta_Q=I_avg*delta_t with delta_t>0; I_avg=-2 A,delta_t=3 s gives -6 C and forward substitution gives -2 A. I_avg=0 at any known positive duration gives unique delta_Q=0. Solve delta_t given delta_Q,I_avg: delta_t=delta_Q/I_avg requires I_avg!=0 and a strictly positive recovered duration (nonzero delta_Q and I_avg must have the same sign). delta_Q=-6 C,I_avg=-2 A gives 3 s and substitutes correctly. If both charge and average are zero, all positive durations are possible; if I_avg=0 with nonzero charge, no finite duration works. If charge is zero with nonzero average, the algebraic result delta_t=0 violates the original domain. Each admissible nonsingular inverse is single valued; no root choice. No reconstruction of a waveform or instantaneous current is possible from this scalar average alone.
limitations: An average alone does not provide instantaneous current, peak current, RMS current, heating or power. Equal units do not authorize binding it to an instantaneous-current input.

An interval of zero duration is undefined. A zero net transfer can result from cancellation, so it does not imply zero energy dissipation. This record supplies no transient evolution, circuit solution or safety guidance.

references.method: Published expected 180 A is retained. The displayed classroom values are evaluated as nominal exact numbers, giving an exact quotient; 1e-10 A permits floating-point noise. This is a textbook arithmetic oracle, not an assertion of measured-input precision or physical uncertainty.
references.provenance: openstax-average-current, Example 9.1(a), 720 C in 4.00 s. No peak or steady-current inference is made.

references.method: Independent unit-count construction: in each of three one-second bins, two one-coulomb packets cross opposite the positive orientation. Each bin has -2 C/s and their duration-weighted mean is -2 A. Total transfer is -6 C. Synthetic exact packets, not an electron-count experiment; tolerance is numerical only.
references.provenance: Curator independent counting derivation from the ampere definition in Eq. 9.2.

references.method: Limiting identity: no net transferred charge over a positive window has zero signed average. Synthetic boundary; does not assert that instantaneous current was always zero.
references.provenance: Curator definitional boundary check; numerical-only tolerance.

rejection_cases.reason: A zero-duration averaging window is undefined, including when transferred charge is also zero.
Duration is defined as positive elapsed time; reverse charge orientation rather than using negative duration.
Transferred charge alone does not identify the averaging duration.

relationship.translation_notes: Local I_avg maps to source I_ave, delta_Q to Delta Q and delta_t to Delta t. Q denotes net charge transported across a chosen section, not the change of charge stored in an unrelated component. C=A*s; division by s gives A, dimension I. No conversion coefficient occurs. Positive orientation is arbitrary but consistent for transferred charge and current; negative values reverse it. Use a new interval-average quantity ID rather than silently binding to the batch-01 steady-current ports. The definition is broader than DC, while the assignment uses its DC-compatible average interpretation without adding a transient solver.

sources.evidence: Average current divides net transported charge by elapsed time. The published starter example reports 180 A; the section distinguishes instantaneous current.
